newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up at 35.64/65 on poor dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up at 35.64/65 on poor dlr demand.

text.p: Indian rupee ended at 35.64/65 per dollar on Tuesday against the opening quote of 35.68/70 on lack of import demand and good dollar supply, dealers said.
The dollar was on the defensive since morning because of poor demand and the two holidays this week, B. Manmadha Rao, manager, forex dealing at Global Trust Bank Ltd said.
Banks were closed for customer transactions on Monday. They are again closed on Wednesday for a national holiday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was in the market buying dollars at 35.65 level, Rahul Mahipal, dealer at brokers Paterson & Co said.
The rupee moved in a 35.65-35.68 range on Tuesday.
The premia on forward dollars fell on rising expectations of easing liquidity on the back of an impending cut in cash reserve requirements for banks, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
RBI officials' remarks on the weekend on India's external balance also helped the rupee appreciate, one dealer said.
An RBI official said on Sunday, India's foreign currency reserves at end-September amounted to $18.4 billion, showing a $1.4 billion increase over the March 1996 figure.
